title: Microsoft Defender for Office 365: submit, block and start automated investigations from advanced hunting
summary: Hold: the briefing overstates what an allow entry bypasses and treats documented permissions, entry expiry and Tenant Allow/Block List auditing as unanswered questions. The roadmap facts and the listed commands match their sources, but administrators need these governance claims corrected before relying on the page.

claims.claim: Tenant Allow/Block List entries govern filtering across the organisation, not just the analyst's mailbox.
claims.quote: Users in the organization can't send email to these blocked domains and addresses.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-office-365/tenant-allow-block-list-about for the organisation-wide filtering statement.

claims.claim: An allow entry added during a false-positive submission lets through mail that filtering had caught.
claims.quote: During mail flow or time of click, if messages containing the entities in the allow entries pass other checks in the filtering stack, the messages are delivered (all filters associated with the allowed entities are skipped).
claims.fix: Replace with: 'An allow entry created during a false-positive submission skips filters associated with the allowed entity; messages are delivered only if they pass the other checks in the filtering stack.'

claims.claim: A block entry prevents delivery of matching mail across the organisation.
claims.quote: Email messages that contain URLs from block entries in the Tenant Allow/Block List are blocked as high confidence phishing. Messages that contain the blocked URLs are quarantined.
